reviews.body:
The fix is right for the reported case, and resolving against the request path is a better model than prefixing the mount point. It also fixes a case the old code got wrong that isn't in the tests: `/doc/subdir/file-a/` (a file with a trailing slash) makes `http.FileServer` send `../file-a`. The old code turned that into `/doc/../file-a`, which a browser resolves to `/file-a`. Now it's `/doc/subdir/file-a/../file-a`, which resolves to `/doc/subdir/file-a`. Might be worth a test row.

One thing to tighten. With a directory mounted at `/`, a request path that starts with two slashes now produces a protocol-relative `Location`. I worked through this from the source rather than running it:

1. A request for `//subdir/nested` keeps `URL.Path` as `//subdir/nested`. `url.ParseRequestURI` only reads an authority after `//` when it isn't parsing a request (`net/url/url.go`, the `viaRequest` check in `parse`).
2. `getServeHandler` matches mounts on `path.Clean(r.URL.Path)`, so it lands on `/`.
3. Mounted at `/`, there's no `StripPrefix`. `http.FileServer` cleans the path, finds the directory `subdir/nested`, and redirects to `nested/`.
4. `fix()` builds `w.reqPath[:LastIndex+1] + v`, which is `//subdir/` + `nested/` = `//subdir/nested/`.

A browser reads `//subdir/nested/` as `https://subdir/nested/`. So a link to `https://node.ts.net//example.com/x` sends the browser to `https://example.com/x/` whenever the served directory happens to contain `example.com/x/`. That's narrow, but it's an open redirect where there wasn't one: before this change the same request went to `/nested/`, which was wrong but stayed on the node.

Collapsing leading slashes on the result would close it without changing anything else:

```go
loc := w.reqPath[:strings.LastIndex(w.reqPath, "/")+1] + v
h.Set("Location", "/"+strings.TrimLeft(loc, "/"))
```

A test row like `{"//subdir/nested", "/", isRedirect("/subdir/nested/")}` would pin it. Mounts below `/` aren't affected, since the result starts with the mount point.

review_comments.body: This leaves dot segments in the header. /doc/subdir/nested/index.html redirects to /doc/subdir/nested/./, and /doc/subdir/file-a/ redirects to /doc/subdir/file-a/../file-a. Browsers resolve both, but a clean path is easier to read in logs and tests. url.URL.ResolveReference on &url.URL{Path: w.reqPath} would do the resolution, remove the dots, and carry the query string. Keep the leading-slash collapse on the next line either way, since URL resolution does not fix //.

I don't think this branch is reachable. http.FileServer only sends relative Locations, and the mount-point redirect for /doc happens before the wrapper. If you keep it as a safety net, a comment saying so would help the next reader. Otherwise it can go, along with the "any other Location" sentence in the doc comment at line 1341.
If the Location gets cleaned per the comment above, this expectation becomes /doc/subdir/file-a. Worth adding the same row for the / mount too: {"/subdir/file-a/", "/", isRedirect("/subdir/file-a")}.

Please add rows for the index.html redirect, which the old code also got wrong below the first level. Something like {"/doc/subdir/nested/index.html", "/doc/", isRedirect("/doc/subdir/nested/")} and the matching row under the / mount. The test setup would need a subdir/nested/index.html file.

comments.body:
Thanks @bcreane. Pushed a follow-up commit:

- `fix()` now resolves the relative `Location` with `url.URL.ResolveReference` against the request path, so dot segments are removed (`/doc/subdir/nested/index.html` -> `/doc/subdir/nested/`, `/doc/subdir/file-a/` -> `/doc/subdir/file-a`) and the query string is carried along. The leading-slash collapse stays on the result.
- The absolute-`Location` branch is kept only as a safety net, with a comment saying `http.FileServer` doesn't produce it; the doc comment no longer mentions it.
- Tests: added `subdir/nested/index.html` to the fixture and rows for the index.html redirect and the trailing-slash file under both the `/` and `/doc/` mounts.

`go test ./ipn/ipnlocal -run TestServeFileOrDirectory` fails on the previous tip (4 rows) and passes now.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Read f14b5b1 against the open-redirect case from earlier, and it still holds. `ResolveReference` keeps a leading `//` from a request like `//subdir/nested`, since the base URL has no host, but the `TrimLeft` runs on the resolved path, so the `Location` still comes out as `/subdir/nested/`. That row is in the table already.

Resolving with `url.URL{Path: r.URL.Path}` also means the decoded path gets re-escaped by `EscapedPath()`. So a directory name containing `%3F` or a space now produces a valid `Location`, where the old string concatenation would have put the raw character back.

One small test gap: the query-string carry-over has no row. `http.FileServer` appends `r.URL.RawQuery` to its directory redirect, so something like `{"/doc/subdir/nested?x=1", "/doc/", isRedirect("/doc/subdir/nested/?x=1")}` would pin it.

Thanks, added the query-string rows: `/subdir/nested?x=1` (mount `/`) and `/doc/subdir/nested?x=1` (mount `/doc/`), both expecting `.../nested/?x=1`. They pass with the current tip of the branch.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
